title: PhilSA moves closer to 2027 rocket launch after South Korea training
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Ten engineers from the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) completed rocket training in South Korea, marking a significant milestone toward the country’s first-ever rocket launch,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Ten engineers from the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) completed rocket training in South Korea, marking a significant milestone toward the country’s first-ever rocket launch, slated for early next year.
The training provided hands-on experience in the assembly, integration and testing of a liquid-fueled sounding rocket under SIKLAB: Building Industrial Space Launch Systems Project.
PhilSA said the initiative is part of its continuing efforts to develop rocket and launch-related capabilities and create opportunities to expand the Philippines’ participation in the space economy.

It said the training highlighted the Philippines’ progress in developing domestic launch capabilities, especially after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said in July, “We are going to launch a rocket into space.”

Following the training, the sounding rocket and ground support equipment will be shipped to the Philippines for final assembly and testing in Cagayan, with the demonstration launch targeted for early 2027.
As Marcos earlier said, “Cagayan is both geographically and economically primed to serve as our gateway to space and host the country’s first spaceport.”

PhilSA Acting Director General Gay Jane Perez said the agency wants the initiative to open doors to succeeding launch activities, attract more commercial interest and create opportunities for Filipino engineers, researchers and enterprises to participate in the growing space economy.
“We want the knowledge gained here to translate into lasting capabilities and contribute to the development of our space industry,” she said, stressing that “our goal goes beyond a single launch.”

The training was held at the Rocket Development Complex of Perigee Aerospace Inc. and covered the entire cycle of Perigee’s Blue Whale 0.1 (BW0.1) sounding rocket, from vehicle assembly to testing and operational preparation.

PhilSA will launch its version of the Blue Whale 0.1, South Korea’s first privately developed liquid-propellant rocket, which was developed by Perigee Aerospace and test-launched on Jeju Island in 2021. /dm
